question: What do one account and one Dagger engine per repository cost on the build VM, and do jobs of one repository still reach another's credentials, environment, engine, Docker or caches?

lab.guest: pinned noble cloud image (kernel 6.8.0-139, systemd 255) under KVM with 8 vCPUs and 11 GiB, provisioned first at the shared-account layout and then migrated by ansible/build-runners.yml with a stub GitHub CLI and a runner archive whose registration and service process are stubbed
lab.deviations: engine slice MemoryMax 8G and runner slice 2G instead of 10G and 4G, because the host had about 12 GB free; the host ran other workloads, including a k3d cluster, throughout

migration.second_apply: changed=0 after the controller clock skew passed

admission.broker: one socket-activated daemon (Accept=no) serving one socket per repository in a root:runner-<repository> 0750 directory
admission.fake_workers: six escaped processes named Runner.Worker in one listener held one lease; a job of another repository was admitted in 49 ms
admission.flood: 32 threads connecting and closing on Y's socket for 20 s: five infra acquire and release round trips took 20-23 ms each, a Y acquire during its own flood 38 ms, no failed units, no broker restarts, broker memory 8 MiB
admission.restart: the broker restarted while a Y job waited with four slots held; the job was admitted 3.0 s later, when a slot was released
admission.systemd_limit: MaxConnectionsPerSource= is not enforced for AF_UNIX peers by systemd 255; the broker bounds open requests per listener unit itself and each repository gets its own socket queue

scanner.layout: db-v2 and java-db-v1 symlinks to one generation each

concurrent_cold_builds.method: infra pipeline image --check-only with the injected CLI, all four at once on empty caches; Go build arguments from the runner environment
concurrent_cold_builds.reading: Cold, four repositories building at once take 9-12 % longer on their own engines, because each engine pulls and unpacks its own base images; engine CPU and the anonymous plus kernel peak stay within 3 % and 0.7 GiB; parallelism 2 is not faster and peaks higher, so parallelism 3 stays
